### 1. Definitions and Context
*   **Pro-$p$ Demushkin Group**: A pro-$p$ group $G$ with a presentation involving $n$ generators $d_1, \dots, d_n$ and a single defining relation $R=1$ such that the relation is "primitive" in a specific sense, allowing the group to be viewed as a deformation of a free pro-$p$ group. These groups are central in the study of pro-$p$ completions of surface groups and 3-manifold groups.
*   **Limit Groups**: A pro-$p$ group is a *pro-$p$ limit group* if it is a limit of free pro-$p$ groups in the pro-$p$ topology. Equivalently, it is fully residually free pro-$p$ (every finite set of non-trivial elements can be distinguished by a map to a free pro-$p$ group).
*   **Residual Freeness**: A group is *residually free pro-$p$* if the intersection of the kernels of all continuous homomorphisms to free pro-$p$ groups is trivial. This is equivalent to being a pro-$p$ limit group.
*   **Full Residual Freeness**: Often implies the stronger condition of being a limit of *free* groups (not just free pro-$p$ groups) or having specific structural properties related to the orientation character.
